candidate.explanation: v22 Final MVP billing-fix candidate, cut 2026-08-29 on branch rc/v22, built on main after the v20 (SV-01) and v21 (SV-21-01) ownership work. SV-22-01 closes the two verified v21 billing-correctness DEFECTS the owner named directly (Prompt 1 of Scalvya_Final_MVP_Fix_Prompts_v22.docx, authorised 2026-08-29). Defect A: migration 039's PARTIAL unique index on customers(app_user_id) WHERE app_user_id IS NOT NULL is NOT inferable as the arbiter for the predicate-less `ON CONFLICT (app_user_id)` PostgREST emits, so the canonical customer upsert would fail under enforcement. New forward-only migration 040_customers_app_user_id_unique_fix.sql fail-closed-preflights duplicate non-null ids, replaces the partial index with a NON-partial single-column UNIQUE index of the same name (PostgreSQL still permits multiple NULL legacy rows), and adds stripe_ownership_uniqueness_ready() which the admin readiness endpoint probes to VERIFY the exact invariant rather than mere column presence; 039 is left in place as historical and never rewritten. Defect B: resolveEntitlement/planFor/isPlanActive now take a stable { userId, email } identity and resolve the local customer via the ONE canonical findCustomerRow (app_user_id under STRIPE_OWNERSHIP_ENFORCED, email before it), fail closed on multiple rows / read errors, and never treat an email-only row as canonical ownership; every authenticated caller (plan gate, account billing display, auth accountStatus, workspace cap, credit gate, and the checkout duplicate-subscription guard) passes req.userId, so an authentication-email change can no longer drop paid access or unlock a second subscription. Migration 038's metadata->uuid backfill was hardened to EXACT UUID validation so one malformed value cannot abort the bounded backfill. Frontend source and the served bundle are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the prior candidate (`git diff 24d350c..7e08768` over app-src/ and app/ is EMPTY; bundle stays index-Cq2NTdSE), so the browser-facing checks are re-observed at this SHA, not reworked. All required checks were RE-RUN at this exact commit 7e08768 in the fail-closed release-candidate workflow on branch rc/v22 (GitHub Actions, 2026-08-29): lint 0/0; unit 1015/1015 (incl. the new REAL-Postgres pglite uniqueness suite proving the 039 partial index fails the onConflict arbiter and 040 succeeds, and the canonical-identity negative/concurrency suite); build; fresh bundle index-Cq2NTdSE; public browser journeys + axe; export rendering; launch integrity; router reachability; dependency audit — every OTHER required job green except the pre-cut freshness gate (which fails by design until this candidate is pinned). The AUTHENTICATED billing matrix was NOT run: the RC's authenticated-e2e job SKIPPED it because the non-production Supabase E2E secrets are not configured (see .github/workflows/release-candidate.yml), so e2e_authenticated is recorded `skipped`, never passed - which makes public_paid NO-GO (capped_beta unaffected). CARRY-FORWARD (valid by this manifest's own standard): `git diff 24d350c..7e08768` over backend/lib/launch-config.js + backend/scripts/release-check.js is EMPTY, so the production config-gate observation carries forward with the standing owner action to re-confirm GET /api/admin/readiness against the deployed 7e08768 before opening paid. OWNER-ONLY, NOT RUN: 7e08768 is not yet deployed; apply migrations 038 -> 039 -> 040, backfill app_user_id, reconcile every ambiguous legacy-map row, then set STRIPE_OWNERSHIP_ENFORCED=1 and run the live current-price A-H money rehearsal. The runtime keeps the legacy email identity path until enforcement is flipped, so the ownership rollout does not itself block paid. public_paid is currently NO-GO for a separate, independent-certification reason - the authenticated matrix was SKIPPED at this candidate (above) - not because of the ownership work; the router-rsc advisory and the live-money rehearsal remain the further conditions once the matrix runs. Documentation-only commits after this SHA (including this launch-state record) do not invalidate the candidate; anything under backend/, app-src/, app/, e2e/, api/ or config does.

drift_from_baseline.subject: feat(billing): complete the deferred Stripe ownership architecture (SV-01/v20)
drift_from_baseline.closes_requirement: v20 SV-01: lands the ownership-architecture trio the owner deferred at v19, additively and with zero runtime behaviour change (978/978 unit tests, incl. all 55 billing/isolation suites; lint 0/0; bundle index-Cq2NTdSE unchanged). ONE canonical typed service lib/stripe-ownership.js (typed states owned/foreign/legacy_mapped/legacy_price/ambiguous/unavailable) that webhooks.js, payments.js and the reconciler delegate to — email/price are never sufficient proof, a conflicting exact+foreign stamp is ambiguous and never adopted. Additive migration 038_stripe_object_ownership.sql (customers.app_user_id + stripe_object_ownership legacy map) with preflight/apply/verify/rollback, plus scripts/backfill-stripe-ownership.js (read-only inventory default, bounded --apply, resume cursor, PII-free receipt) and docs/RUNBOOK_STRIPE_OWNERSHIP.md. OWNER-ONLY, NOT RUN: apply migration 038; run the backfill and reconcile every ambiguous row; then sunset the price-only fallback (each fallback use is measured by legacy_price_ownership_fallback). This does NOT advance public_paid to full GO and does NOT freeze a new candidate — v20 changed backend code and added migration 038, so a new RC must be cut before the pinned candidate moves past 24d350c.

drift_from_baseline.subject: test(e2e): run authenticated matrix single-worker for a deterministic gate (v18)

migrations.on_disk_note: 40 numbered migrations plus two unnumbered files that are deliberately NOT part of the applied set: CHECK_APPLIED.sql (a verification query) and E2E_MARKER.sql (the seeding opt-in, which must be run against a non-production database only). The applied range is still 001-037: 038_stripe_object_ownership.sql (SV-01/v20), 039_stripe_ownership_enforcement.sql (SV-21-01/v21) and 040_customers_app_user_id_unique_fix.sql (SV-22-01/v22) are on disk but NOT YET APPLIED — all owner-only, additive and reversible. 038 adds customers.app_user_id + the stripe_object_ownership legacy-map (its metadata->uuid backfill was hardened in v22 to EXACT UUID validation so one malformed value cannot abort the bounded backfill). 039 created a PARTIAL unique index on customers(app_user_id) WHERE app_user_id IS NOT NULL — which the v22 audit found is NOT inferable as the arbiter for the predicate-less `ON CONFLICT (app_user_id)` PostgREST emits, so the canonical upsert would fail under enforcement (Defect A). 040 is the forward-only correction: it fails-closed-preflights duplicate non-null ids, replaces the partial index with a NON-partial single-column UNIQUE index of the same name (a valid arbiter; PostgreSQL still permits multiple NULL legacy rows), and adds stripe_ownership_uniqueness_ready() which the readiness endpoint probes to VERIFY the exact invariant rather than mere column presence. Apply order is 038 → 039 → 040 (039 is left in place as historical; 040 supersedes its index). Their preflight/apply/verify/rollback are in each file header. Until the owner applies 038+039+040, backfills app_user_id, reconciles every ambiguous legacy-map row and sets STRIPE_OWNERSHIP_ENFORCED=1, the runtime keeps the existing price-only legacy fallback and all three migrations stay pending owner actions (see docs/RUNBOOK_STRIPE_OWNERSHIP.md and GET /api/admin/readiness ownership.state, which now fails closed on a missing/partial uniqueness arbiter).

how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".

3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each. A check whose underlying code changed since the last candidate may NOT be carried forward — re-run it or mark it not_run.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.

Any commit after step 2 that changes code creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO. Documentation-only commits (docs/ and the prompt packs) do not.
